1) Olivia/Jacob: confirm whether AurumPay intends Redwood to be the Processor for customer-derived PII, or if you foresee any joint-controller use cases. This determines SCC module choice.
2) Please send your vendor SQ — we'll start filling it and loop Rishi for any legal-only questions.
3) If you want SOC 2 evidence, we can share our Type II attestation under NDA; Rishi can advise timeline.
4) If helpful, schedule a 30-min legal sync next week to align on DPA/SCC and subprocessors.

Attaching the two files we discussed. Let me know which times work for a legal sync (I can coordinate).

Hi Tessa — thanks for the clear recap and materials. Quick notes from AurumPay legal/privacy side: 

- AurumPay will be the Controller for our customer payment data; we expect Redwood to act as Processor.
- We typically ask processors to sign the EU DPA and the Controller->Processor SCC module; happy to review your suggested language.
- SOC 2: we're required to see either a current SOC 2 Type II or an attestation timeline. We don't need the full report immediately but will require it before production onboarding.
- Data residency: currently most of our customers are EU-based; we'd like to understand if Redwood can offer EU-only processing for selected customers.

I've attached our vendor security questionnaire (Aurum_Vendor_SQ.pdf). Please have your security team fill the main sections and we can follow up on technical details. Also please send your DPA draft and any SCC guidance.

Can we tentatively schedule a legal sync on Thu 28 Aug between 09:00-11:00 CET? If that works, we'll invite our legal lead.

Best,

Subject: Re: AurumPay — follow-up: DPA requirements, SCC module options, controller/processor alignment

Tessa — looping in legal and privacy owners here with a short recommended approach you can share with AurumPay.

Short guidance:
1) Controller/Processor: Based on your note that AurumPay is Controller for customer payment data, Redwood should be the Processor. We will not accept a joint-controller posture for standard onboarding where we only perform inference/serving.

2) SCC module: Recommend the EU Standard Contractual Clauses Module for Controller -> Processor transfers (commonly referred to as Module 2 in our contracting playbook). That mapping aligns with AurumPay's ask and avoids joint-controller complexity.

3) DPA: We'll provide our standard DPA template with the Processor obligations and optional EU addendum. I attached an initial draft for AurumPay (Draft_DPA_AurumPay_v1.docx). Please note: the DPA will include subprocessors list and a subprocessors notification process; if AurumPay requires prior-approval for subprocessors, flag that now so we can confirm feasibility.

4) SOC 2: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II attestation. We can share the attestation under an NDA and provide a redacted report or SOC2 summary. If AurumPay needs the full report for procurement, we'll request an NDA and then provide the file.

5) Data residency: We support region-based routing; we can route EU tenant data to EU-only clusters where requested but this will be handled as part of Dedicated/Private options or a contract annex. If they require EU-only processing for a subset of customers, we should document the scope and discuss cost/SLAs.

Next steps you can propose to AurumPay:
- Confirm Controller->Processor alignment and whether they need prior-approval subprocessors clause.
- Share the vendor SQ back to us; we will assign security to complete technical sections.
- NDA for SOC 2 share if they want the attestation.
- Legal sync to review DPA draft (Thu 28 Aug 09:00-11:00 CET looks workable; Rishi and Marissa can join).

If they push for SCC alternative language, escalate to Lauren for any contract exceptions.

Rgds,
Rishi Malhotra
